plain_description.what: Each match is judged in both orders. Across all certified caches, it looks at cases where the verdict flipped with order, and measures what share favoured whichever answer was shown first, per benchmark and judge.
plain_description.why: A tool-use benchmark (BFCL) showed flips going entirely one way. The question was whether that kind of position bias is general.
plain_description.information: If one-sided flips are general, dual-order judging is needed everywhere and the BFCL pattern is not special. Result: done. All five supported families showed one-sided flips, but in opposite directions by judge: grok favours the first answer, Mistral the second. The general conclusion rests on MATH, only slightly above even, from one of its two caches. BFCL's total one-sidedness is not typical. It says nothing about why judges prefer a position or about individual matches. The MMLU-Pro caches come from the older question pool, later ruled history rather than evidence; the BFCL part is not affected.
